salient_findings: Pulsatile mass in the epigastric region
key_facts: 84-year-old man with medical history of hyperlipidemia, hypertension, hypothyroidism, and tobacco use
20-pack-year smoking history
Smoking pipe tobacco for the past 10 years
Asymptomatic abdominal mass with pulsations
Vital signs: Temperature - afebrile, Blood pressure - 120/76 mm Hg, Pulse rate - 73 beats/min, Respiratory rate - 16/minute
Pulses were palpable in the lower extremities bilaterally
Complete blood count and electrolyte levels were within normal limits
Computed tomographic angiogram (CTA) of abdomen and pelvis showed a saccular aneurysm
Aneurysmal neck angulation greater than 60 degrees with neck tortuosity noted
Dense calcifications of iliac vessels present without narrowing
No signs of impending rupture

shortlist.label: Abdominal aortic aneurysm
shortlist.why_kept: Large pulsatile mass in epigastric region with soft bruit and imaging showing saccular aneurysm

shortlist.label: Inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysm
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of dense calcifications and aneurysmal neck angulation greater than 60 degrees

shortlist.label: Aortoiliac occlusive disease
shortlist.why_kept: History of smoking and hypertension, which are risk factors for aortoiliac occlusive disease

shortlist.label: Takayasu arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: Large vessel vasculitis that can cause aneurysms and is more common in older adults

shortlist.label: Fibromuscular dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause aneurysms and is more common in older adults with a history of smoking

raw.rationale: The patient's 20-pack-year smoking history, age, and presence of a large pulsatile mass in the epigastric region with a soft bruit audible on auscultation, along with the CTA showing a saccular aneurysm, strongly support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysm
rejected.why: There is no mention of inflammatory markers or symptoms suggestive of an inflammatory process

rejected.label: Aortoiliac occlusive disease
rejected.why: The presence of a large pulsatile mass and the CTA findings are more consistent with an aneurysm than occlusive disease

rejected.label: Takayasu arteritis
rejected.why: This condition is more common in younger women and the patient's age and sex do not fit the typical demographic

rejected.label: Fibromuscular dysplasia
rejected.why: This condition is more common in younger women and the patient's age, sex, and the presence of a large aneurysm do not fit the typical presentation
